plain: To decide a matter officially, as a judge would

webster.text: To decide, or determine, in the case of a controverted question; to decree by a judicial opinion; used appropriately of courts of law and equity.

example.quote: If the reasons that can be given against an act are such as plainly demonstrate that it is against natural equity, the executive courts will adjudge such act void.
example.cite: James Otis, The Rights of the British Colonies Asserted and Proved (Boston, 1764)
